correctness.rationale: The event that an index is an upper record is uniform among preceding positions and independent of unordered values. For i>a and j<=a, conditioning on record status fixes the maximum at i but leaves the first i unordered threshold count binomial with mean i q, yielding covariance -(1-q)(1-(1-q)^(i-1))/[i(i-1)]. For i<=a the record indicator is independent of the symmetric first-a threshold count. Summing yields the exact finite formula; binomial mixing uses independence of relative rank permutation and coordinate order statistics. A telescope controls its error and proves the fixed-p,q asymptotic. The checker independently enumerates all rank permutations through n=7 and checks 199 exact mixed cells and the bound on an exact rational grid through n=34.

originality.rationale: The evaluated theorem is the exact covariance of planar Pareto-maxima count with a northeast-threshold occupancy count, its conditional sign, and universal exponential-limit constant. Bentley et al. derive mean maximal counts from relative rankings; Bai et al. analyze marginal planar-maxima limit laws. Their inspected available primary full texts do not imply the displayed mixed conditional covariance. Records and rank independence alone are prior tools; the new calculation is the nonzero interaction of two threshold filters. Historical risk from uninspected broad joint-process formulas is retained.

value.rationale: The overlap of two natural coordinate-threshold events has a nontrivial sign of covariance with total Pareto-frontier size even though each coordinate-threshold count, separately and jointly as a pair, is independent of the frontier size. Formula (1) classifies every sample size and all conditional exceedance counts, while the universal fixed-threshold limit -(1-p)(1-q) has a quantitative exponential error. The result is a motivated exact interaction statistic, not a marginal mean restatement or a small numerical gain.
